name: runner-human-qa-helper
purpose: Canonical contract for agents populating Runner's human QA helper with artifact-bound questions, checklists, notes, verdicts, and Visuals evidence.
applies_when: a human visual or behavioral judgment is required
a deterministic QA path reaches a documented human-QA handoff
an agent asks the user to review screenshot or video evidence
an agent requests product-direction, visual-quality, usability, or interaction feedback

exact_identity.visual_identity: Include Visuals evidence_ids and/or run_id whenever visual media exists.
stale_when: the relevant evidence set is replaced

overall_verdict.note: Overall verdict is separate from targeted questions; do not use a generic targeted question as a substitute.

rules: Ask one concrete judgment per question.
Tie every question to an acceptance criterion, known ambiguity, or product decision.
Use plain language and describe what to look at or try.
Ask only for human judgment the agent cannot prove deterministically.
Do not ask the user to verify tests, status codes, source identity, deployment identity, logs, or other facts the agent can verify.
Do not ask generic questions such as 'does this look good?' when a more specific visual or interaction criterion exists.
Put blocker or decision-critical questions first.
Do not repeat the same criterion in both a question and checklist item unless one is judgment and the other is an observable prerequisite.

checklist.preferred_items: 3-6 when the review has multiple observable conditions
rules: Use checklist items for observable states or steps the user can confirm by looking or interacting.
Keep each item short enough to scan while the preview is visible.
Do not turn deterministic assertions into user checklist work.
Do not require a checklist for a truly single-criterion review.
Group or order items in the sequence the user will naturally inspect them.

derive_from: exact preview route and interaction path
required_behavior: Populate the helper before asking the user to review.
Generate the questions/checklist for the user; do not ask the user to author them.
Attach exact evidence and artifact identity.
Include deterministic evidence as context, not as homework.
If there is no meaningful human judgment left, do not manufacture a human-QA request.

review_lifecycle.notes: Freeform user notes attach to the exact reviewed artifact/evidence receipt.
review_lifecycle.answers: Question and checklist responses attach to the exact packet version.
review_lifecycle.invalidation: A stale artifact/evidence identity preserves historical answers but they no longer authorize or satisfy review for the new identity.
review_lifecycle.async_media: The packet may be registered while media is queued/uploading, but visual criteria are not human-proven until the referenced media or live preview is actually viewable.
review_lifecycle.no_gate_bypass: Human QA never overrides mandatory tests, security gates, branch protection, or other deterministic policy.
